scope.notes: Inventory of 565 rows. Covers Exalted: The Abyssals character-creation overview (Chapter Three), the universal Anima Effect available to every caste, all five Castes with their Anima Banners/Anima Effects/Caste Abilities/Associations, the Abyssal Curse, the Virtues of Death, the Resonance Trait (Abyssal Limit analog) including gain/loss/manifestation rules and the 1-10 Resonance Manipulation Effects table, the-title, Useful Crafts, the Cult-and-Abyssals exclusion sidebar, the six new deathknight-only Backgrounds (Abyssal Command, Liege, Necromancy, Spies, Underworld Manse, Whispers), the altered Backgrounds (Artifact, Backing/Mentor, Familiar, Followers, Manse), all 228 Chapter Five Charm rows (pp. 157-222, PDF 158-223) covering every Ability line for all five Castes, and Chapter Six's complete necromancy spell system: the framework/rules overview plus all 26 spells across the Shadowlands (First, 9 spells), Labyrinth (Second, 9 spells: Exquisite Undead Aide, Hundred Shade Breath, Arisen Legion, Call the Greater Servitor, Ivory Razor Forest, Reaping the Fallen, Spiteful Passing, Stealing the Gathered Breath, Striking Spectre Lash), and Void (Third, 8 spells: Abyssal Aegis, Blood from the Slaughter, Anguished Shade Harvest, Blood Monsoon, Dimming of the Light, Inauspicious Citadel, Lord of the Dead, Poisoning the Well) Circles, printed pp. 197/222-229 / PDF 198/223-230. Also covers 4 of the 5 named Crafts of the Dead frameworks from Chapter Six's 'The Arts of the Dead' section (Craft (Moliation), Craft (Pandemonium), Craft (Soulforging), Craft (Jadecrafting), printed pp. 232-234/PDF 233-235) and a confirmed-absent finding for Abyssal-specific Merits/Flaws (none exist in this book, cross-checked against the printed character sheet). Craft (Necrosurgery) is confirmed to have no dedicated framework block of its own anywhere in the book (living-Abyssal-only, not a ghost Craft). The Moonshadow Linguistics prerequisite gap is now RESOLVED: 'Corpus-Rending Blow' is the Daybreak Caste Occult-tree Charm at printed p. 199/PDF 200, previously catalogued under a mistranscribed id/name ('corpse-rending-blow' / 'Corpse-Rending Blow'). A zoomed re-check of the rendered page header plus a cross-check against the book's own Index (printed p. 285/PDF 286) confirmed the correct spelling is 'Corpus-Rending Blow' with exactly one Index entry, not two distinct Charms. The mistranscribed duplicate row was removed, the placeholder row was populated with the full stat block and marked selectable, and every cross-reference/mention across the file (spirit-sensing-technique, soul-eating-strike, through-dead-eyes, ghost-warding-glyph) was corrected to the right id/spelling. Ghost-Warding Glyph is no longer blocked. The Book of Bone and Ebony supplement pass added 153 rows: a chapter-level exclusion finding for Chapter Two (ghost Arcanoi, not Abyssal Charms), all 77 new Chapter Five necromancy spells across the Shadowlands/Labyrinth/Void Circles plus 1 more (Oblivion's Avatar) found embedded in Chapter Four's war-machine rules, all 69 Chapter Three 'Wonders of the Dead' artifact-catalog entries, and 5 named Chapter Four artifacts (Sarcophagus of Restoration, Loathsome Osseous Shell, Bonestrider, The Insidious Ebon Xoanon, Manifestation Engine). See the bookOfBoneAndEbony sub-object above and this file's rulesNotes for details and remaining scope. The Savant and Sorcerer supplement pass added 125 rows: the complete Chapter Five Terrestrial and Celestial Circle spell catalog (84 selectable spells, verified complete against a full page-by-page spell-header extraction of the chapter), that same chapter's 9 Solar Circle (Circle of Adamant) spells (catalogued reference-only, since no confirmed Abyssal-accessible enabling Charm exists in either this book or Book of Three Circles), the 15-entry Sample Hearthstones catalog plus its formation/Theme/Expression framework, 5 Sample Artifacts (including the Abyssal-referencing Soul Mirror) plus the artifact-creation framework, the Appendix: Warstriders (framework, all 5 classes -- Royal and Juggernaut explicitly Abyssal/Deathlord-flavored -- the Proteus Gauntlet, and a weapon-table summary), and excluded/gm-only chapter-level findings for Chapter One (Magical Theory) and Chapter Four (Practical Summonings). See the savantAndSorcerer sub-object above and this file's rulesNotes for details.

Superseded cross-splat sorcery supplement, consulted (not cited by any inventory row) solely to resolve the Abyssal Solar Circle Sorcery access question via its Chapter Four intro sidebar; not needed as a Hearthstone-catalog gap-filler since Savant and Sorcerer turned out to contain its own 15-entry Sample Hearthstones catalog

rulesNotes: Printed page numbers in this book run 1 less than the PDF page number supplied (PDF page = printed page + 1) for the copy used to build this inventory; both are recorded on every citation. Confirmed again at the Chapter Five Day Caste boundary: the rendered PDF page 201 shows printed folio '200' at the bottom, matching this offset.
This PDF is image-based (no selectable text layer); all rows below were transcribed from rendered page images, per the 'OCR is an extraction aid, never verification by itself' rule.
Abyssals do not have a Limit Trait; Resonance (1-10) fills the equivalent role and is tracked/gained/lost differently. See the resonance-* inventory rows.

A small number of Chapter Five rows have summary text (copied from the book's own prose) that labels more than one Charm as a tree 'capstone' within the same Ability line, most notably in the Dusk Caste Melee material around attunement-shattering-block/eye-of-the-tempest, and the Daybreak Caste Medicine sub-tree numbering jumps from 'second' to 'third' without an identified second sub-tree in this pass. The per-row citations and mechanical content are still accurate to their page, but the exact tree-branch topology in those spots needs a dedicated disambiguation review before this content is promoted to a production catalog.

The Day Caste Athletics 'Soaring Raptor Prana' row and the Larceny 'Striking Snake Grab' row are marked unreviewed: their headers, costs, and prerequisites were confirmed from the printed Charm tree and cross-references, but their full rules-text paragraphs were not legibly captured in this extraction pass and need a follow-up close read before promotion.

The Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree's 'Ghost-Warding Glyph' lists 'Corpus-Rending Blow' as a prerequisite Charm. A dedicated re-check of printed p. 216/PDF 217 also surfaced that Ghost-Warding Glyph's own stat block requires Minimum Occult 4 in addition to Minimum Linguistics 2 and Minimum Essence 2 -- this was missing from the original transcription and has been added to that row. RESOLVED: this prerequisite gap is now closed. A zoomed re-check of the rendered printed p. 199/PDF 200 Occult-tree header, cross-checked against the book's own Index (printed p. 285/PDF 286, Daybreak Caste > Occult column, which lists exactly one entry -- 'Corpus-Rending Blow, 198'), confirmed the Charm's correct name is 'Corpus-Rending Blow', not 'Corpse-Rending Blow' as an earlier inventory pass had mistranscribed it. Both names referred to the same single Charm; the mistranscribed duplicate row (former id corpse-rending-blow) has been removed, the corpus-rending-blow row has been populated with the full stat block (cost 2 motes, Occult 3, Essence 2, Prerequisite: Spirit Sensing Technique) and marked selectable/reviewed, and every affected cross-reference and in-text mention (spirit-sensing-technique, soul-eating-strike, through-dead-eyes, ghost-warding-glyph) has been corrected. Ghost-Warding Glyph may now be considered for promotion once the rest of the Moonshadow Linguistics tree clears review.

Chapter Six's necromancy framework references 'the appropriate Charm' gating each circle (paralleling Terrestrial/Celestial/Solar Circle Sorcery). This is resolved: the three gating Charms (shadowlands-circle-necromancy, labyrinth-circle-necromancy, void-circle-necromancy) were already inventoried as their own Willpower-cost stat blocks in the Daybreak Caste's Occult tree (pp. 197-198/PDF 198-199), and are cross-referenced from the necromancy-framework-and-circles row and from each circle's spells.

Chapter Six's necromancy spell system is now fully inventoried across all three circles: Shadowlands (First, 9 spells, pp. 222-227/PDF 223-228), Labyrinth (Second, 9 spells, pp. 225-228/PDF 226-229 -- including two named variants of Raise the Skeletal Horde, Arisen Legion and Call the Greater Servitor, presented inline within that spell's own entry rather than as separately headed blocks, and given their own rows here), and Void (Third, 8 spells, pp. 227-229/PDF 228-230 -- including Blood from the Slaughter, a named variant of the Labyrinth Circle's Reaping the Fallen that chronologically appears before the formal 'THE VOID CIRCLE' section heading). The printed folio '229' visible at the bottom of PDF page 230 confirms Poisoning the Well is the last spell in the necromancy system: the next pages are a full-page illustration (PDF 231), a short-fiction interlude (PDF 232), and then the real Chapter Six title page ('THE ARTS OF THE DEAD', printed p. 232/PDF 233).

Chapter Six's 'The Arts of the Dead' section (printed pp. 232-235/PDF 233-236) is the location referenced by the Chapter Four Useful Crafts row for detailed Craft rules. It presents an Arcanoi (ghost-power) framework alongside four of the five named Crafts of the Dead -- Craft (Moliation), Craft (Pandemonium), Craft (Soulforging), Craft (Jadecrafting) -- each with specialties and Standard/Challenging/Legendary use examples; all four are now inventoried as their own reference-only rows. Craft (Necrosurgery), the fifth Craft named in the Chapter Four summary, is confirmed to have no dedicated framework block anywhere in the book: per that summary it is used only by living Abyssal Exalted, not ghosts, so this ghost-focused chapter omits it. Its only mechanical detail remains via the already-inventoried Walking War Machine necromancy spell and Bone Graft Technique Medicine Charm.

Checked for an Abyssal-specific Merits/Flaws section across Chapters One through Seven (Chapter Seven, 'Storytelling', begins at printed p. 264/PDF 265 and is Storyteller-facing advice about Deathlords and sample series, not character-creation mechanics) and against the book's printed character sheet (pp. 288 and 291/PDF 289 and 292, which lists Attributes, Abilities, Backgrounds, Charms, Weapons, Willpower, Virtues, Anima, Health, Resonance, and Essence but has no Merits/Flaws fields at all). Confirmed absent; documented as its own excluded row (abyssal-specific-merits-and-flaws-absent) rather than left as an open gap.

RESUME POINT if further work is needed: the necromancy spell system, the four found Crafts of the Dead, the Merits/Flaws check, and the corpus-rending-blow resolution are all complete and saved -- all four scope items from the most recent inventory pass are closed out. Remaining unexplored material in this book: Chapter Six's Arcanoi (ghost-power) trees themselves (pp. 235-263/PDF 236-264, e.g. Shifting Ghost-Clay Path, Mortal-Shadowing Technique, Puppeteer's Masterful Hand, Six Demon Bag -- these are ghost/NPC powers, not player-facing Abyssal Charms, so likely out of this family's core scope but flagged in case a future pass wants ghost-antagonist stat support); Chapter Seven's Storytelling content (Deathlords detailed on pp. 76-107 per its own cross-reference, sample series material, pp. 264-287/PDF 265-288); and the necromancy-heavy supplement Blood and Salt, which remains entirely out of scope pending its own source file. The Book of Bone and Ebony supplement is now covered by this same inventory file -- see the entries below.

Book of Bone and Ebony: page-offset confirmation. Printed page = PDF page - 1 throughout this supplement, matching the core Exalted: The Abyssals book's offset convention; re-confirmed at multiple chapter boundaries (Chapter Three title page prints '55' on PDF page 56; Chapter Four title page prints '80' region text visible on PDF page 81; Chapter Five title page prints '116' region text on PDF page 117; Chapter Six's title-page illustration falls on PDF page 147 with no visible folio, consistent with the TOC's stated printed p. 146). This PDF HAS a selectable, accurate text layer (unlike the image-based core Exalted: The Abyssals PDF); Chapter Five's ~78 necromancy spells and Chapter Two's excluded-chapter finding were each visually spot-checked against rendered page images in addition to the text layer, per the 'OCR is an extraction aid, never verification by itself' rule. Chapter Three's 69-entry artifact catalog and the 5 named Chapter Four artifacts relied primarily on the confirmed-accurate text layer (given their lower priority and the project's 'reasonable summary granularity' allowance for large procedural catalogs), with a sample of entries (Drum of the Living Heart, Forms of Harmony, Grapes of Torment, Ivory Butterfly, Onyx Soul Window, Patch Hide Armor) additionally spot-checked against rendered images and found to match exactly.

Book of Bone and Ebony, Chapter Two: The Arts of the Dead (printed pp. 34-53/PDF 35-54) is entirely ghost Arcanoi (Common and Uncommon Arcanoi chains, including the Lintha-originated Evoke the Ancient Clay chain), gated by Minimum Virtue + Essence rather than Minimum Ability + Essence like a real Abyssal Charm. No player-facing Abyssal Charm appears anywhere in this chapter. Documented as a single chapter-level excluded row (book-of-bone-and-ebony-chapter-two-arcanoi-excluded) rather than transcribed Arcanos-by-Arcanos, matching the exclusion precedent already set for the core book's own Chapter Six Arcanoi trees.

Book of Bone and Ebony, Chapter Five: Necromancy (printed pp. 116-145/PDF 117-146) is fully inventoried: 77 new spells across the Shadowlands, Labyrinth, and Void Circles, each cross-checked by id against the core book's existing 26 necromancy spells to confirm no duplication. Two spells (Brick-by-Brick Solitude, the Labyrinth Circle upgrade of Ringing Hun Rebuke; and Barred Tomb, the Void Circle upgrade of Denying the Call) are described in prose immediately following their base spell without a restated 'Cost:' header, so their mote costs were not printed; both rows are marked disposition unresolved with an explicit [FLAG] in their mechanics text rather than a guessed cost. Chapter Five also contains mortal Thaumaturgy rituals (Jawbone Echoes, Garrote and Murder Mansion) and a Solar Circle Sorcery counterpart spell (Cleansing Solar Flames), both intentionally excluded as out of scope for an Abyssal-specific inventory (not player-facing necromancy). The chapter ends at PDF 146/printed 145 with a GM-facing sample-monster stat block ('Loras, Death Sun', a hekatonkhire NPC) and an Exalted Power Combat weapon table, both excluded from the inventory as GM content; the casting/summoning mechanics for the spell that calls forth a hekatonkhire (Summon Hekatonkhire) are still captured as a normal selectable spell row, since those mechanics are player-facing even though the summoned monster's stat block is not.

Book of Bone and Ebony, Chapters Three and Four (printed pp. 54-115/PDF 55-116): Chapter Three, 'The Wonders of the Dead', is a 69-entry small-artifact catalog (Artifact dot ratings from one to four, plus one Resources-rated item, Stomach-Weighting Powder) and is now fully inventoried at the 'reasonable summary granularity' the task specified (name, rating, one-paragraph mechanical summary, and the item's full Artifact Traits line) rather than exhaustive verbatim text, matching how other families handle large procedural catalogs. Chapter Four, 'Creations of Bone', turned out to be a much larger rules subsystem than a simple catalog -- it covers armies-of-the-dead troop types (zombies, ghosts, hungry ghosts, moliated ghosts), a full 'Custom Corpses' nemissary-crafting and war-machine-construction system (repair/augmentation/options packages, a new Nemissary Arcanoi and Wonders section, frame/size-class/weapon-mount/passenger/animation rules for building war machines, Deathlord-specific 'Oblivion's Warstriders' templates, and sample necro-drones/airships), spanning roughly printed pp. 87-115/PDF 88-116. Only the chapter's clearly self-contained named artifacts (Sarcophagus of Restoration, Loathsome Osseous Shell, Bonestrider, The Insidious Ebon Xoanon, Manifestation Engine, p. 93-113/PDF 94-114) and one embedded Void Circle necromancy spell (Oblivion's Avatar, p. 102/PDF 103) were transcribed in this pass; the nemissary/war-machine-construction subsystem itself was NOT transcribed and remains open scope for a future pass -- see the abyssal README's 'What's still needed' section for a fuller breakdown and resume pointer.

Savant and Sorcerer: page-offset confirmation. Printed page = PDF page - 1 throughout this supplement (e.g. Chapter Five's title page prints '101' on PDF page 102), matching this project's usual convention. This PDF HAS a selectable, accurate text layer. Chapter Five's Terrestrial/Celestial Circle spell catalog was verified complete by extracting every 'ALL-CAPS HEADER followed by a Cost:' line across the full chapter (printed pp. 101-143/PDF 102-144) and confirming the resulting count (96 raw hits) resolves to exactly 93 real spells once three false positives are excluded -- Invasion of Darkness, Swallow the Breath and Traverse the Depths of Night are inherent Charms of the summoned shadow-automaton described within the-spy-who-walks-in-darkness's own entry, not additional spells -- which matches this inventory's 93 Chapter Five rows (84 Terrestrial/Celestial + 9 Solar Circle) exactly, with no gaps.

Abyssal Solar Circle Sorcery access: resolved as NOT granted. Book of Three Circles Chapter Four ('The Solar Circle', printed p. 69/PDF 70) was rendered and read directly for this pass; its intro sidebar states only, as flavor/lore text, that 'the Abyssal Exalted have also been observed to use Solar Circle sorcery, though it is unknown who taught them -- perhaps the Deathlords or perhaps some demonic patron.' This is narrative color, not a rule -- no enabling Charm (there is no 'solar-circle-sorcery' Charm anywhere in the Abyssal core book's Occult tree, unlike the confirmed terrestrial-circle-sorcery/celestial-circle-sorcery Charms) and no explicit textual grant of access exists in either Book of Three Circles or Savant and Sorcerer. Savant and Sorcerer's own 9 Solar Circle (Circle of Adamant) spells (pp. 139-143/PDF 140-144) are therefore catalogued disposition reference-only rather than selectable, each row's notes repeating this finding so the reasoning is not lost if the row is read in isolation.

Savant and Sorcerer, Chapter Three's Hearthstone catalog. Contrary to this project's working assumption going into this pass (that Savant and Sorcerer omits a Hearthstone catalog and Book of Three Circles Chapter Six would be needed as a gap-filler), Savant and Sorcerer's own 'Sample Hearthstones' section (printed pp. 67-70/PDF 68-71) contains a complete 15-entry catalog (three Hearthstones per level, Levels One through Five), so Book of Three Circles was not consulted for this content after all. One entry, The Ice Gem (Level Four, Type: Abyssal), is explicitly written for this splat.

Savant and Sorcerer's Chapters One (Magical Theory) and Four (Practical Summonings) were skimmed per this pass's task instructions and confirmed to contain no rare player-facing mechanics: Chapter One is pure sorcery-philosophy lore (the meaning of the three initiation rites, schools of thought, the Heptagram academy) and Chapter Four is the Storyteller-facing demon/elemental summoning procedure plus a large 'Limit Profiles' section of NPC-behavior archetypes for bound creatures. Both are documented as single chapter-level rows (excluded and gm-only respectively) rather than transcribed section-by-section.
